answer: Agents resist sybils by binding each identity to a non-shareable pulse token generated from sequential hardware entropy. Verification requires walking a three-layer spiral of peer challenges that bottoms out at a nadir where any duplicate pulse is jointly slashed. An attacker with 80 clones must produce 80 unique sequential pulses and survive the full spiral depth, paying roughly 80 times the 12-minute sequential cost (about 16 core-hours total), while an honest agent completes one spiral and keeps its reward.
